title: The Two Largest Neighbors
problem: The numbers 1 through 10 are arranged uniformly at random in a row. What is the probability that 9 and 10 are adjacent?

hints.text: Condition on the position of 10, or fuse 9 and 10 into a block.
A fixed pair is adjacent in a random permutation of n items with probability 2/n.

solution.setup: Treat 9 and 10 as a two-item block with two internal orders.
solution.reasoning: The block plus the other eight values gives nine objects, arranged in 9! ways, and the block has two orders. There are 2·9! favorable permutations out of 10!, so the probability is 2/10.
solution.sanityCheck: The value 10 has on average fewer than two neighboring positions near the row ends, leading to an adjacency probability below 2/9 and exactly 1/5.

keyInsight: Block counting converts adjacency into an ordinary permutation count.
recognitionCues: Two distinguished objects must occupy consecutive positions in a random ordering.
commonMistakes: Using 1/10 and forgetting the two internal orders.
followUps: What if the arrangement is circular?
